source: Conventional emergency-fund coverage bands as they appear in mainstream personal-finance guidance (CFPB, FINRA, and the Financial Order of Operations' 3-6 month rung). Rules of thumb, not law — kept in data/ so the bands can be edited without touching the engine.
confidenceNote: Coverage bands are rules of thumb from mainstream guidance, not law.
note: SPEC.md Section 13, Tier 1.5 SWAN Number. These bands exist ONLY to give a self-reported number some context. The SWAN Number is deliberately feeling-based: a band is never a verdict, and the room must not tell someone their own number is wrong. Bands are expressed in months of monthly expenses and are checked lowest-to-highest, so the first band whose maxMonths the value falls at or under wins; the last band has no maxMonths and catches everything above.

bands.label: A starter cushion
bands.blurb: About a month of expenses — enough to absorb a surprise bill without reaching for a card.

bands.label: The usual floor
bands.blurb: Three months is where most guidance starts, and where the Financial Order of Operations puts its first full emergency-fund rung.

bands.label: The usual full fund
bands.blurb: Three to six months is the range named most often, and the top of it suits a single income or variable pay.

bands.label: Deliberately deeper
bands.blurb: More than most guidance calls for. Common with self-employment, commission pay, a specialised job market, or anyone supporting other people.

bands.label: A year or more
bands.blurb: Well past what any rule of thumb asks for. That is allowed — cash you hold for peace of mind is buying something the return on it does not measure.
